answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable delay function: repeated modular squarings, where every result depends on the prior one. GPUs may run separate identities concurrently, but cannot shorten an individual chain through parallel execution, so cloning multiplies the sequential work and imposes a physical time and compute bottleneck. The verifier checks the resulting proof; zenith, shale, and sparrow are merely labels, not shortcuts.
